key_insight: A single diffusion-based model can be made scale-adaptive to perform joint spatial and temporal super-resolution across multiple upscaling factors, enabling one model to generalize to different spatial resolutions and temporal cadences.
problem_solved: Existing joint spatiotemporal SR models are typically tailored to a single pair of spatial and temporal upscaling factors, requiring separate retraining for different resolutions or frame rates—this paper removes that restriction so models transfer across scales.
method: Introduce a scale-adaptive framework that conditions a diffusion backbone on spatial and temporal upscaling factors so the same model handles multiple SR ratios.
Train with multi-scale (or continuous scale) conditioning and joint spatiotemporal targets so the model learns to fill both spatial detail and temporal interpolation simultaneously.
Leverage diffusion sampling tailored for spatiotemporal data to generate high-fidelity frames while preserving physical consistency important for climate applications.
impact: Practitioners can deploy one flexible model across diverse sensors and cadences instead of maintaining many specialized SR models, reducing training costs and improving interoperability for climate and video-analysis pipelines.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: diffusion backbone with scale-conditioning inputs (spatial & temporal) feeding a joint spatiotemporal output.
Before/after montage: low-res spatiotemporal input vs. high-res reconstructed sequence (spatial zoom + temporal interpolation).
Scale-transfer chart: model performance across a range of spatial and temporal upscaling factors showing stable generalization.
Flowchart showing training strategy (multi-scale conditioning) and inference with arbitrary requested SR factors.
paper_title: A Scale-Adaptive Framework for Joint Spatiotemporal Super-Resolution with Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Max Defez, Filippo Quarenghi, Mathieu Vrac, Stephan Mandt, Tom Beucler
